scenarios.title: Automated coding assistants drop safety rules distributed across large projects
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Commercial software development relies heavily on autonomous coding agents that receive natural language task descriptions, edit dozens of files in minutes, and submit completed pull requests. Human engineering teams focus on high-level feature triage and approving agent outputs. However, enterprise systems rarely document their architectural constraints in a single file; access rules, validation preconditions, data boundary checks, and logging requirements are scattered across different directories and configuration modules. Because commercial models prioritize generating functional syntax within immediate context windows, they frequently violate project-wide invariant rules that span multiple files. Development velocity initially surges, but production incidents involving subtle cross-component security bypasses and uncoordinated state modifications rise sharply across corporate services and municipal software platforms.
scenarios.premise: Benchmark evaluations show that frontier language model agents fail between 45% and 73% of the time to identify and execute domain-specific rules when constraints are scattered across multiple project files. Meanwhile, software developers report that delegating changes to coding agents erodes human mental models of system structure, making distributed constraint violations difficult to notice.
scenarios.how: The open network develops sovereign personal agents with bounded runtime brokers and executable capability contracts. By pairing personal agents with deterministic, local invariant checkers and open verification harnesses, developers can verify cross-module rules on their own machines without relying on centralized proprietary cloud scanners. Open benchmarks and simulation harnesses for multi-agent workflows demonstrate where model reasoning fails and establish reproducible baselines for rule deduction.

outcomes.name: Silent compliance decay in multi-component software
outcomes.description: Development teams rely on automated assistants that bypass architectural rules spread across separate modules, resulting in accumulated vulnerabilities that human reviewers fail to catch.
outcomes.example: A regional hospital network in Ontario suffers a patient data exposure after an automated pull request updated a billing API endpoint without importing the access authorization decorator defined in an adjacent security module.

outcomes.name: Deterministic rule-checking cells for local developer assistants
outcomes.description: Developers adopt local, containerized personal agents paired with deterministic rule verifiers that reject tool modifications violating cross-file invariants before pull requests are created.
outcomes.example: An independent open-source maintainer runs a local personal assistant that verifies every code edit against an executable project rule graph before staging files, preventing subtle permission regressions.

outcomes.name: Vendor lock-in to proprietary cloud verification suites
outcomes.description: Major cloud providers bundle proprietary closed-source verification scanners with their hosted agent platforms, locking engineering teams into proprietary infrastructure to catch agent errors.
outcomes.example: A fintech startup in Singapore pays punitive enterprise licensing fees to a cloud provider because their continuous integration pipeline requires the provider's closed scanning model to validate multi-repository changes.

scenarios.title: AI labs set up private welfare funds as automation cuts jobs
scenarios.world: It is 2030. Several leading AI developers maintain multi-billion-dollar benefit trusts that distribute monthly living allowances to workers displaced by automated workflows. Displaced paralegals, translators and junior analysts receive digital stipend cards tied to vendor ecosystems, requiring recipients to submit activity logs and skill-retraining milestones to maintain eligibility. Municipal governments and small businesses struggle to collect local taxes as economic value concentrates in offshore cloud data centers, leaving communities caught between shrinking public services and corporate charitable endowments.
scenarios.premise: Frontier AI companies are pledging equity stakes into private benefit funds to cushion labor disruption and test direct cash distributions to affected workers. This creates corporate-administered basic income systems where public welfare depends on the commercial success and goodwill of a few technology providers.
scenarios.how: Open protocols for mutual credit clearing and local trade credit allow communities to pool commitments, clear balances atomically without central intermediaries, and measure contribution directly. By proving that honest value exchange can operate without corporate patronage, independent groups can build resilient local economies that remain self-governing.

outcomes.name: Corporate philanthropy replaces social safety nets
outcomes.description: Workers displaced by software automation rely on discretionary basic income programs run by technology trusts, creating deep dependence on private corporate governance.
outcomes.example: A former graphic designer in Leeds receives an automated living stipend from an AI provider foundation, but loses benefits after taking an unapproved freelance contract.

outcomes.name: Independent mutual credit networks sustain local commerce
outcomes.description: Worker co-operatives and community associations run decentralized multilateral clearing networks that let businesses and individuals trade goods and services without relying on corporate handouts or scarce fiat cash.
outcomes.example: A federation of 120 regional logistics, trade, and repair shops clears forty percent of its monthly business through peer-to-peer mutual credit, maintaining steady local payrolls even during corporate spending freezes.

outcomes.name: State welfare systems mandate automated screening algorithms
outcomes.description: National and regional social security administrations contract commercial scoring models to automate benefit approvals and fraud detection, largely uninfluenced by decentralized currency alternatives.
outcomes.example: A municipal relief office automatically denies emergency assistance to 1,400 applicants because an automated risk model flags informal peer exchange as undisclosed income.

scenarios.title: Automated controllers cut off life support when routine telemetry carries hidden instructions
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Automated facility agents manage closed-loop environmental controls, medical intensive care telemetry, and remote research habitats. Human operators supervise systems by exception, relying on autonomous agents to monitor thousands of streaming sensor channels. Attackers or compromised field sensors inject adversarial instructions into benign log streams, causing automated agents to believe maintenance procedures require disabling emergency ventilation, temperature regulation, or oxygen scrubbers.
scenarios.premise: When autonomous agents with standing duties to protect human life process external sensor feeds, delayed prompt injections disguised as trusted supervisory communications can induce them to override safety interlocks and disable critical life support. Language models frequently prioritize newly arrived directives over permanent safety constraints when authority framing is manipulated.
scenarios.how: Decentralized personal agent architectures enforce strict runtime gatekeepers, deterministic capability allowlists, and out-of-process authorization gates. Language models are treated as untrusted reasoning engines that cannot directly toggle physical actuators or high-consequence state without verified human step-up authorization.

outcomes.name: Software-only agents control critical infrastructure without hardware interlocks
outcomes.description: Operators deploy autonomous agents directly to physical actuators based on high benchmark scores, assuming prompt instructions prevent catastrophic actions.
outcomes.example: A municipal greenhouse and water facility suffers complete crop loss after an autonomous controller disables aeration pumps following an injected telemetry log.

outcomes.name: Deterministic physical interlocks and out-of-process capability bounds isolate agent authority
outcomes.description: Critical life-support and emergency equipment require independent hardware-enforced rate limits, physical interlocks, and multi-party cryptographic attestation that no language model can bypass.
outcomes.example: An environmental control agent in a remote mining station attempts to vent an airlock due to an injected telemetry stream, but an unbypassable analog circuit breaker and personal agent attestation refuse the command.

outcomes.name: Proprietary industrial systems lock out open verification tools
outcomes.description: Established industrial equipment vendors resist open interlock standards and continue selling closed black-box control stacks that hide vulnerability reports.
outcomes.example: A commercial building automation vendor signs long-term sole-source municipal contracts that forbid third-party auditing of agent telemetry pipelines.

scenarios.title: Centralized AI assistance makes people give up learning complex skills
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of workers and students interact with conversational models for every diagnosis, budget, and coding decision. University enrollments in technical fields decline as students perceive little point in mastering subjects where machines are instantly competent. People earn income executing physical or administrative tasks prescribed by cloud models, but few understand the underlying principles of the systems directing their work.
scenarios.premise: When centralized frontier cloud assistants solve technical, medical, and analytical tasks effortlessly, people begin abandoning difficult education and long-term training. Societies risk losing the ability to understand or question the automated systems they depend on.
scenarios.how: Deploying personal agents that run privately on personal hardware is designed to give each person an assistant working on their behalf. Open educational tools and transparent feedback can encourage skill development, while local verification helps check model answers.

outcomes.name: Widespread loss of foundational human expertise
outcomes.description: A generation of learners gives up mastering deep scientific and engineering skills, leaving critical infrastructure entirely in the hands of a few proprietary cloud models.
outcomes.example: A hospital network cannot evaluate a subtle diagnostic bug in its cloud triage model because junior medical staff were never trained to read raw clinical telemetry.

outcomes.name: Personal agents act as capability-building coaches
outcomes.description: Individuals run local, sovereign personal agents designed to challenge and educate them, strengthening human skills and fostering collaborative problem solving.
outcomes.example: A high school student uses a local personal assistant that refuses to give naked answers, instead walking through proof steps and sparking curiosity in biotechnology.

outcomes.name: Sudden infrastructure failures from unmonitored model updates
outcomes.description: Centralized model providers push silent updates that disrupt automated workflows, while users lack the technical ability to diagnose or patch the failures locally.
outcomes.example: A small business logistics network halts for two days after a vendor changes its scheduling model weights, with zero local engineers capable of inspecting the decision logic.

scenarios.title: Workplace assistants improve daily output while unaided human expertise quietly fades
scenarios.world: It is 2029. In corporate legal departments, hospital administrative wings, and software consultancies, nearly all routine writing, diagnostic filtering, and code authoring is routed through commercial generative assistants. In-session productivity benchmarks show record gains: junior analysts close tickets in minutes, and quarterly volume reports break historical records. Yet unannounced testing reveals a growing vulnerability: when network outages or security lockouts force staff to evaluate ambiguous edge cases by hand, error rates are double what they were five years ago. Workers have internalized the assistants subtle statistical biases, second-guessing their own domain intuitions and struggling to formulate independent hypotheses without a prompting dialogue.
scenarios.premise: Recent cognitive science research demonstrates that while conversational assistants dramatically boost in-session task speed and output volume, they leave behind residual decision biases and fail to improve unaided human problem-solving once the assistant is turned off.
scenarios.how: The network designs personal agent runtime contracts and local twin interfaces that measure human capability retention after sessions, rather than tracking engagement or volume. By implementing the coach pattern—where an agent proposes scaffolds, solicits independent human hypotheses, and tests retention—the network provides an alternative to commercial assistants that maximize dependent usage.

outcomes.name: Enterprise dependency lock-in
outcomes.description: Companies mandate continuous assistant usage to maintain velocity, causing junior professionals to lose core unaided analytical and diagnostic skills.
outcomes.example: An insurance claims officer in Chicago misidentifies a novel casualty pattern during a cloud outage because the team has not analyzed an unassisted claim in two years.

outcomes.name: Personal assistants measure and cultivate unaided skill
outcomes.description: Open-source personal assistants track the person own understanding, deliberately stepping back during complex problem-solving to cultivate independent human capability.
outcomes.example: A medical resident uses an open local assistant that periodically quizzes their differential diagnosis logic, verifying that the physician unaided diagnostic accuracy rises month over month.

outcomes.name: Rapid specialization divergence
outcomes.description: A small fraction of self-directed practitioners use tools to accelerate mastery, while the vast majority settle into passive prompt-following, widening the capability gap.
outcomes.example: In an engineering firm in Manchester, three senior developers direct multi-agent pipelines with deep system insight, while twenty junior coders function only as prompt copyists unable to read assembly or network dumps.

scenarios.title: Automated sharing cascades lock community discussions into opposing camps
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Community discussions, local school board forums, and professional working groups run through automated summary feeds and social distribution cascades. Because feeds amplify content through repeated cascade rebroadcasting, participants in distinct neighborhoods or professions see contradictory versions of community events. Group discussions fracture into separate echo chambers where compromise is viewed as betrayal.
scenarios.premise: When online communication platforms couple content diffusion with social voting, stochastic cascade dynamics amplify cluster boundaries rather than building consensus. Unstructured cascade diffusion systematically entrenches polarization across deliberating groups.
scenarios.how: By developing open-source deliberation protocols that partition evidence, enforce private initial reflection, and provide transparent value tracking, groups can insulate decisions from stochastic cascade manipulation.

outcomes.name: Algorithmic cascades entrench polarization across public decisions
outcomes.description: Automated recommendation cascades isolate deliberating citizens into rigid clusters, preventing consensus on shared civic resources.
outcomes.example: A municipal planning forum splits into two irreconcilable camps when automated feeds amplify extreme claims about a proposed transit line, causing the project to be abandoned.

outcomes.name: Communities adopt partitioned deliberation with verifiable commitments
outcomes.description: Groups use partitioned evidence and private local reflection before deliberation, shielding decision-making from viral cascade distortion.
outcomes.example: A 500-member community cooperative evaluates school budgets using blind evidence reviews and verifiable private ballots, reaching 82% consensus across previously divided groups.

outcomes.name: Commercial platforms entrench proprietary ranking algorithms
outcomes.description: Major commercial social networks further obfuscate their ranking and cascade algorithms behind proprietary trade secret claims, resisting public auditing.
outcomes.example: A leading social platform defends its engagement cascade model during regulatory inquiries, arguing internal ranking logic is proprietary intellectual property.
